statements.quote: To increase the ease of maintaining and extending the system, we built an API (Application Programming Interface) to separate the client-side user interface logic from server-side processing logic.
statements.locator: Earlier system paper, arXiv:2311.01937v1 (3 Nov 2023), not the target c357 experimental article; PDF p. 4, section 4.1 Implementation, second paragraph; markdown line 155.

statements.quote: We expect this API-based approach to also be valuable in making the Supermind Ideator moves available to others who might want to build upon or extend our methodology beyond the initial web interface we have provided. The API simplifies each move into a simple set of text strings with most of the formatting and interaction with OpenAI’s GPT models abstracted away to optional parameters. We elaborate upon how to use the API in the Appendix.
statements.locator: Earlier system paper, arXiv:2311.01937v1 (3 Nov 2023), not the target c357 experimental article; PDF p. 4, section 4.1 Implementation, third paragraph; markdown lines 157-159.

statements.quote: While the general knowledge embedded within GPT’s base model can produce interesting and fitting output with relatively limited guidance (zero-shot and few-shot prompts), it seemed apt to augment this base knowledge with specialized information so that more precise and useful ideas could also be generated. To accomplish this, we curated approximately 1600 examples of real-world organizational practices that solved problems using various innovative approaches. We organized this case study corpus with input labels that connected the problem and case study with an associated Cognify or Groupify move.
statements.locator: Earlier system paper, arXiv:2311.01937v1 (3 Nov 2023), not the target c357 experimental article; PDF p. 4, section 4.2 Fine-Tuning, first paragraph; markdown line 163. Describes training examples, not participant data.

statements.quote: This enabled us to fine-tune GPT so the new model could map between input language, output prediction, and Supermind move. This new fine-tuned model is much less constrained than our zero-shot and few-shot moves. While these earlier moves answer a question or problem with another question or idea based on the base GPT model and our prompting, the fine-tuned approach changes the GPT prediction model so that output more tightly reflects the input training data. As our training data was a corpus of case studies, the fine-tuned model produces output more akin to those case studies. This produces an interesting challenge and opportunity as the GPT system tends to produce fictional content in a coherent and sensible manner, reading as if it is stating facts.
statements.locator: Earlier system paper, arXiv:2311.01937v1 (3 Nov 2023), not the target c357 experimental article; PDF p. 4, section 4.2 Fine-Tuning, second paragraph; markdown line 165.

statements.quote: All study activity occurred remotely through online meetings which averaged about 45 minutes in length. The researcher ran a think-aloud protocol with each participant, first explaining the Supermind Ideator application, and then asking the participant to suggest a problem statement to kick off the session. As the system generated ideas, participants were asked to reflect on and respond to the output. As this was a formative study, we collected (a) UX insights related to which aspects of the application ’made sense’ to participants and which did not, and (b) measures of professional applicability, such as where and how participants might make use of the application in their professional lives.
statements.locator: Earlier system paper, arXiv:2311.01937v1 (3 Nov 2023), not the target c357 experimental article; PDF p. 5, section 5 Evaluation, second paragraph; markdown lines 187-189. Describes formative-study data collection, not public availability.

statements.quote: While we have not yet demonstrated this capability, the structure of the Ideator suggests how a specialized front end and flexible back end can help create a platform for community creation and evolution. Collective software development by an open-source community, for example, can improve or add individual “moves” or run combinations of moves within custom UIs. We hope that our contribution scaffolds future design and development of tools that augment the collective ability of many others.
statements.locator: Earlier system paper, arXiv:2311.01937v1 (3 Nov 2023), not the target c357 experimental article; PDF p. 6, section 6.4 Community-based extension; markdown line 223.

statements.quote: It appears that the Ideator has the potential to provide substantial assistance to humans doing creative problem-solving. Much work remains to be done for this potential to be fully realized, and more complete, quantitative evaluations of factors such as the user experience of people using the system and the speed and quality of the ideas they generate are currently underway. We also see at least three short-term paths forward to improve Ideator:
statements.locator: Earlier system paper, arXiv:2311.01937v1 (3 Nov 2023), not the target c357 experimental article; PDF p. 6, section 7 Future Work, opening paragraph; markdown line 227. Quantitative evaluations were still underway in this version.

statements.quote: We hope that by having an extensible and open-source API for the Supermind Ideator, communities of professionals, researchers, consultants, and others could contribute to a growing collective of knowledge about how to guide LLMs to help with specific types of ideation and creative problem solving.

notes:
Checked 2026-10-09 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without authentication. The complete local markdown was read in three chunks (394 lines; 47,984 characters), including all references and Appendix A; PDF text on pages 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 9 was also extracted for verification.

Critical source mismatch: retrieval.json associates this candidate with C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Heyman et al (2024) - Supermind Ideator.md and the corresponding PDF. PDF page 1 identifies arXiv:2311.01937v1, 3 Nov 2023, Supermind Ideator: Exploring generative AI to support creative problem-solving, first authors Steven R. Rick and Gianni Giacomelli. This is not the target journal article, Supermind Ideator: How scaffolding Human-AI collaboration can increase creativity, DOI 10.1177/26339137241305117. The 40-person formative study in section 5 of the local PDF is not form study S1. Every quotation in statements is explicitly located in this earlier document; none is attributed to the inaccessible target article.

No data availability, data-on-request, preregistration, or supplementary-file statement and no study-data or source-code repository link was found in the complete earlier document. The quotations retain its related API, training-corpus, collected-data, open-source, and materials descriptions. The approximately 1600 case examples are a training corpus, not experimental participant observations. Appendix A provides a prompt example and parameter documentation, not participant records. Statements about an open-source API express intentions; they do not identify a public code deposit.

Target publisher landing page https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/26339137241305117 returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot check; stopped. The article's supplementary-material links and target availability statement could not be inspected. Target Crossref record https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1177/26339137241305117 returned HTTP 200, confirming title/authors and the experimental abstract; it provided no related data identifier. The separately linked ACM conference article https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3643562.3672611 also returned HTTP 403 with a bot check; stopped. These access failures concern articles and do not establish restricted access to any c357 data deposit.

The cited software URL https://ideator.mit.edu/ returned HTTP 200 but only the JavaScript application shell ('You need to enable JavaScript to run this app.'); no downloadable research-data file or repository link was exposed. The cited methodology page https://cci.mit.edu/supermind-design-primer/ returned HTTP 200 and links to general primer PDFs from 2020 and 2021. These are not deposits for the target experiment. Its publications link https://cci.mit.edu/publications/ returned HTTP 200 and lists the journal, conference, and earlier arXiv papers without a data-deposit link. The arXiv landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01937 returned HTTP 200 and shows only the 2023 v1 submission. A publication, general methodology primer, and application shell are not counted as target-study deposits.

Excluded author-search lead: https://osf.io/km2zq/ (HTTP 200) and https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/km2zq/ (HTTP 200), titled Generative Idea Diversity and Area of Exploration, by Jennifer Heyman and Steven R. Rick. DataCite metadata at https://api.datacite.org/dois/10.17605/osf.io/km2zq returned HTTP 200. Registration response 72-7 explicitly describes a 2x2 mood-board experiment about 'a chair for children', citing DOI 10.1145/3582269.3615596, rather than the three-arm Supermind Ideator experiment. Its statement that the dataset is not publicly available therefore cannot be applied to c357. Its linked project https://osf.io/yr2we/ returned HTTP 200 for the site shell, while https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/yr2we/, https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/yr2we/files/osfstorage/, and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/yr2we/children/ each returned HTTP 401, 'Authentication credentials were not provided.' No authentication or further access was attempted. Neither this unrelated registration nor its private project is included in deposits.

No deposit was confirmed to cover form study S1. No participant/output file was downloaded and no row count, column set, arm assignment, outcome score, or participant text was available to inspect. The form's data_and_code URLs are empty, and the current form contains no final.open_items field. Consequently no missing per-person or arm mean, SD, SE, analyzed count, effect size, or diversity measure can be computed from the public sources confirmed here. what_we_could_compute is null.

Confidence is low because the source on file is the wrong version and the target full text and publisher supplement listing remain unavailable. none_found reports the outcome of these searches, not proof that the data were never shared. An unrelated private dataset is not grounds for marking c357 restricted. No GitHub repository is named in the local paper and no GitHub API request was made. Only the requested output JSON was written; all network responses were held in memory.
